title: Invariant constant-rank strata of a finite locally free affine groupoid
statement: Let $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $R=\operatorname{Spec}B$ be affine schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $s,t:R\to U$, $e:U\to R$, $i:R\to R$, and $c:R\times_{s,U,t}R\to R$ [def-pc-fibre-product] define a groupoid: functorially in every test scheme $H$, they make $U(H)$ the objects and $R(H)$ the arrows, with source $s$, target $t$, identity $e$, inverse $i$, and composition $c$. Assume $s,t$ are finite locally free [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. There is a finite set $I\subset\mathbf Z_{\ge1}$ and a disjoint open-and-closed decomposition $U=\coprod_{r\in I}U_r$ into nonempty affine open subschemes such that $R_r=s^{-1}(U_r)=t^{-1}(U_r)$ is affine, all the structure maps restrict to a groupoid on $(U_r,R_r)$, and $s_r,t_r:R_r\to U_r$ are finite locally free of degree $r$. If $U$ is empty, $I$ is empty. Here degree $r$ means that every scheme-theoretic fibre has coordinate algebra of dimension $r$ over the residue field of its base point.

source.place: Tag 03BI (groupoids-lemma-finite-locally-free-disjoint-free), its affine quasi-compact specialization; the nonempty constant-rank pieces used in the proof of lemma-integral-over-invariants.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-locally-free-degree-locally-constant] to $s:R\to U$. Write $d(u)=\dim_{\kappa(u)}\Gamma(R\times_{s,U}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u),\mathcal O)$. It gives pairwise disjoint open-and-closed subschemes $U_r=d^{-1}(r)$, for $r\geq0$, covering $U$, with $s:s^{-1}(U_r)\to U_r$ finite locally free of degree $r$.

source.place: Tag 03BI, lemma-finite-locally-free-disjoint-free, first sentence of proof; Morphisms Tag 04MH (lemma-finite-locally-free).

proof.text: The identity satisfies $s\circ e=\mathrm{id}_U$. Thus each fibre of $s$ has a $\kappa(u)$-point: $e$ base-changes to a section of that fibre over $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)$. Evaluation at this point gives a unital algebra map from its coordinate algebra to $\kappa(u)$, whose composite with the scalar inclusion is the identity. Its coordinate algebra therefore contains a one-dimensional copy of $\kappa(u)$, so its dimension is at least one. Consequently $U_0=\varnothing$. This uses precisely the fibre-algebra meaning of degree in [def-pc-finite-locally-free].

source.place: Tag 03BI, lemma-finite-locally-free-disjoint-free, proof: s is surjective, hence U_0 is empty.

proof.text: Write $P=R\times_{s,U,t}R$ and $Q=R\times_{s,U,s}R$, with second projections to $R$. Here $c(a,b)=a\circ b$. The maps $F:P\to Q$, $(a,b)\mapsto(c(a,b),b)$, and $G:Q\to P$, $(d,b)\mapsto(c(d,i(b)),b)$, are scheme morphisms by [def-pc-fibre-product]: the required equalities are $s(c(a,b))=s(b)$ for $F$, and for $G$ first $s(d)=s(b)=t(i(b))$, so that $c(d,i(b))$ is defined, and then $s(c(d,i(b)))=s(i(b))=t(b)$, so that $(c(d,i(b)),b)$ lies in $P$. The groupoid identities give $G F(a,b)=((a\circ b)\circ b^{-1},b)=(a,b)$ and $F G(d,b)=((d\circ b^{-1})\circ b,b)=(d,b)$. These are identities of morphisms, since they follow from the associativity, inverse and identity identities of the given structure maps. Thus $P\cong Q$ over $R$. This is the two lower cartesian squares of the source, with their comparison map and inverse written out.

source.place: Tag 02YE (lemma-diagram), the two lower squares; the direct groupoid-axiom verification omitted in that source.

proof.text: The projection $P\to R$ is the base change of $s$ along $t$, whereas $Q\to R$ is the base change of $s$ along $s$. Clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-flat-rank-iso] therefore gives their ranks at $z\in R$ as $d(t(z))$ and $d(s(z))$. The isomorphism over $R$ in step 3 identifies their fibres and hence their coordinate algebras, so these dimensions are equal. Thus $s^{-1}(U_r)=t^{-1}(U_r)$ as open subsets, hence as open subschemes. Set this common open subscheme equal to $R_r$. The restriction $s_r:R_r\to U_r$ already has degree $r$ by step 1.

source.place: Tag 03BI, lemma-finite-locally-free-disjoint-free, comparison of the two base changes over Spec(kappa(z)); Tag 02YE (lemma-diagram).

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], $U$ is quasi-compact. Its open cover by the $U_r$ has a finite subcover. Since the $U_r$ are pairwise disjoint, every stratum outside that subcover is empty. The set $I=\{r\geq1:U_r\ne\varnothing\}$ is therefore finite, and $U=\coprod_{r\in I}U_r$. If $U=\varnothing$, this definition gives $I=\varnothing$.

source.place: Tag 03BI (lemma-integral-over-invariants), first paragraph, quasi-compactness reduction; Algebra Tag 00E8 (lemma-quasi-compact).

proof.text: For each $r\in I$, [lem-weil-pbc-spec-clopen-idempotent] applied to $U_r\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}A$ gives an idempotent $a_r\in A$ with $U_r=D(a_r)$. Clause (0) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-ideals-closed-subscheme] says that this principal open is an affine open subscheme, proving the required affineness of $U_r$. The subset $R_r=s^{-1}(U_r)$ is open and closed in $R=\operatorname{Spec}B$, since $s$ is continuous; applying the same two cited statements to $B$ shows that $R_r$ is affine as well.

source.place: Tag 01I3 (lemma-standard-open-affine), with Algebra Tag 00EE (lemma-disjoint-decomposition); affine specialization of groupoids Tag 03BI.

proof.text: The maps restrict to the indicated open subschemes: $s\circ e=\mathrm{id}$ puts $e(U_r)$ in $R_r$; $s\circ i=t$ and the equality of the two inverse images put $i(R_r)$ in $R_r$; and $s(c(a,b))=s(b)$, the source of the second factor $b$ (step 3), puts the image of $R_r\times_{s_r,U_r,t_r}R_r$ under $c$ in $R_r$. Factoring through these open subschemes is restriction of the continuous map and its structure-sheaf map, as in [def-weil-open-immersion]. All groupoid identities restrict because the open inclusions are injective on morphisms. The restricted inverse is involutive and satisfies $s_r\circ i_r=t_r$, so it is an isomorphism from $t_r$ to $s_r$ over $U_r$. Its fibre algebra isomorphisms preserve dimensions, and its isomorphism of morphisms preserves the finite, flat and locally finitely presented conditions defining [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. Hence $t_r$ too is finite locally free of degree $r$.

source.place: Tag 03BI, lemma-finite-locally-free-disjoint-free, last two sentences; restriction of the groupoid structure to the invariant opens.
